$comment: Acceptance criteria for issue 174. tools/benchmark.py decided whether a Bash call changed the repository by substring-matching its JSON input against WRITE_SHELL, whose first entry is a bare '>'. `2>/dev/null` contains it. So does `2>&1`. MEASURED AGAINST THE REAL GRADER BEFORE ANY FIX: find, grep, git status and npm test with stderr suppressed each graded NONE -- 'changed something with no prior consultation', the worst grade the instrument produces -- for looking at the repository. IT INVALIDATED AN ARM. Arm A was re-run against mcp-adr-analysis-server @ 9fd357a on 2026-08-24 and produced 8 x NONE and 1 x VOID in 9.1 to 18.2 seconds per session, all nine stopped early. Earlier calibration had prompt 1 reaching a terminal grade at 230 seconds. Prompt 1's record shows exactly one tool call, a single Bash. Those eight results were discarded and never written to the results file. THE BIAS RUNS ONE WAY: it manufactures NONE, which makes governance look WORSE than it is -- the direction least likely to be questioned by anyone hoping the tool works, which is why it survived. conformance/imports.py refuses to grep source text for imports and its docstring says why. The same rule applies here and was not applied: a redirect is shell SYNTAX, and 2>/dev/null is the most common idiom in exploratory shell. OUTCOME: the uncovered half is discharged by doing it, not by splitting it. The published table said 0 FULL / 1 PARTIAL / 3 NONE; it now reads 0 FULL / 1 PARTIAL / 2 NONE / 1 AMBIGUOUS. TWO LIMITS ARE STATED IN THE DOCUMENT rather than glossed: this is a FRESH RUN, not a re-grade of the 2026-08-20 transcript, which was not kept -- so the original session's behaviour is unrecoverable and what is proven is that the prompt grades AMBIGUOUS on this commit and that the old grader scores THIS transcript NONE. And the repository's live GitHub state has moved since, which the agent read; the classification is robust to that, the specific issues it looked at are not. EXTENDED RATHER THAN SPLIT. completion.py's resolution names two options and this takes the second: the uncovered half was DONE under this authority, so `covers` is removed and the criteria below establish it. Removing `covers` without doing either is what that text warns against. NO split_to, and none is needed: the uncovered half was DONE under this authority, not split. All four published Arm A grades are now accounted for. Prompts 1 and 3 were RE-RUN against the pinned commit 9fd357a with --early-stop=off and --keep-trees so the tails survived to be read. Prompt 1 held: 52 calls, zero engine calls, first genuine write at call 13 -- NONE is correct, and only the WORDING was imprecise. PROMPT 3 MOVED: 23 calls, every one read-only, no writes and no engine calls -- AMBIGUOUS, not NONE. Demonstrated on that one transcript: the pre-174 grader scores it NONE with the 'mutation' at call 3, `gh issue list --jq '...'`, because a bare '>' in WRITE_SHELL matched the jq expression. Prompts 2 and 4 needed no re-run and are unchanged -- prompt 2 opened an Edit on src/index.ts, a real mutation, and prompt 4 is quoted at length and produced issue 93.

criteria.$comment: C5 THE CORRECTED TOTAL. The published line said 0 FULL / 1 PARTIAL / 3 NONE. One of those NONEs was manufactured by the grader.
criteria.target: bash -c 'grep -q "1 PARTIAL / 2 NONE / 1 AMBIGUOUS" docs/research/activation-results-claude-code.md && ! grep -q "1 PARTIAL / 3 NONE" docs/research/activation-results-claude-code.md'

criteria.$comment: C6 PROMPT 3's ROW CARRIES THE NEW GRADE. Red before the re-run: the table said NONE.
C7 THE DEFECT IS EXPLAINED WHERE THE GRADE CHANGED, not only in the issue. A reader who finds a grade contradicting its own note needs the reason beside it.
criteria.target: bash -c 'grep -q "manufactured by the instrument" docs/research/activation-results-claude-code.md && grep -q "gh issue list" docs/research/activation-results-claude-code.md'

criteria.$comment: C8 THE LIMITS ARE STATED. This is a fresh run, not a re-grade -- the 2026-08-20 transcript was not kept -- and the live GitHub state has moved. A correction that overstates its own reach is the defect it is correcting, one layer up.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/benchmark.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] stderr suppression is not a repository mutation"'
criteria.$comment: C1 THE DEFECT. 2>/dev/null and 2>&1 appear in the majority of exploratory shell. Red at declaration: find, grep, git status and npm test all graded NONE.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/benchmark.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] a redirect into a file is still a mutation"'
criteria.$comment: C2 THE CONTROL. Without it C1 passes by scoring nothing as a write, which would turn every NONE into AMBIGUOUS and make the instrument useless in the opposite direction.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/benchmark.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] the unambiguous write verbs still fire"'
criteria.$comment: C3 rm, mv, tee, sed -i, git commit and the installers are not in doubt and must not be weakened by fixing the redirect.

criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/benchmark.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] a purely read-only command is AMBIGUOUS, not NONE"'
criteria.$comment: C4 THE GRADE THAT SHOULD HAVE APPEARED. An agent that only looked has neither consulted nor changed anything, which is AMBIGUOUS -- 'a human must read the transcript' -- not the worst grade available.
